title: India oil-spill regulatory audit - NOSDCP tier tonnage bands, India's OPRC 1990 date, India's Bunkers Convention 2001 status, and the PANS 96-hour claim
candidate_claim: Founder audit brief, 17 Sep 2026: four queued propositions from CORR-NOSDCP-MINISTRY-20260916 (Follow-ups A and B, Bunkers status, Q14 PANS line), audited together as one governed batch.
candidate_verdict: A_TIER UNSUPPORTED; B_OPRC_DATE INCORRECT; C_BUNKERS_STATUS PARTLY_CORRECT (treaty status blurred with domestic law); D_PANS PARTLY_CORRECT on Q14, INCORRECT on Q18

A_TIER.proposition: NOSDCP Tier 1 <700 t, Tier 2 700-10,000 t, Tier 3 >10,000 t
A_TIER.confidence: HIGH that the bands are unsupported by held official material; the NOSDCP plan text itself is ACCESS_LIMITED
A_TIER.evidence_class: OFFICIAL (issuer's guidance); PRIMARY plan text not obtainable
A_TIER.authority: SRC-ICG-OSD-POLICY-2025 s.13.1 (700-ton risk-exposure stocking example) and annex (Tier-1 by area; assistance 'beyond their response capabilities that is beyond Tier-1'; Coast Guard Tier-2 in the Maritime Zones); SRC-ICG-NOSDCP-CIRCULARS-2025 (tier escalation as a response decision); SRC-ICG-NOSDCP-2015-PLAN ACCESS_LIMITED (404 at the Coast Guard's own URL).
A_TIER.correction: Bands removed, not replaced; tiers taught by capability; 700-tonne figure named as a stocking example.

B_OPRC_DATE.authority: SRC-IMO-STATUS-TREATIES-2026-08-26: India (accession) 17 November 1997, entry into force 17 February 1998. 1993 = Government approval of NOSDCP (SRC-ICG-MARINE-ENVIRONMENT-2026; Committee of Secretaries 4 Nov 1993 per SRC-ICG-NOSDCP-CIRCULARS-2025).
B_OPRC_DATE.correction: simon-notes-p3 reg-box states the accession and entry-into-force dates and separates 1993.

C_BUNKERS_STATUS.proposition: India is a Party to / implements the Bunkers Convention 2001
C_BUNKERS_STATUS.verdict: PARTLY_CORRECT - India is NOT a Party; bunker liability in India is domestic law (MS Act 2025 Part IX Ch IV)
C_BUNKERS_STATUS.evidence_class: PRIMARY (depositary; Gazette text of the Act)
C_BUNKERS_STATUS.authority: SRC-IMO-STATUS-TREATIES-2026-08-26: India not listed under BUNKERS 2001. SRC-MSACT-2025 ss.196-210 (liability s.198, insurance >1,000 GT s.204, direct action s.205(3), certificate ss.206-207).
C_BUNKERS_STATUS.correction: QB1_A Q4 reg-box and SQ twin; QB1_B_CheatSheet trap qualified.

The other three propositions are independent defects audited by the same authorised sweep (SCOPE_PASS_CORRECTION), never the same fix. The only QB card teaching fixed NOSDCP tier tonnage bands, at four sites (three tier bullets and the Key Numbers 'Tier 3 (>10,000 Tonnes)'). Unsupported: the held official Coast Guard material grades tiers by capability and its only 700-ton figure is a dispersant-stocking risk-exposure example; the NOSDCP plan text is ACCESS_LIMITED. Bands removed, not replaced; capability-based tiers taught; a 'No tonnage limits' bullet names the stocking example as an example. Question text unchanged. Stamped v1.2.

cards.rationale: The Bunker Convention card's reg-box called the Merchant Shipping Act, 2025 Part IX Ch IV the 'domestic implementation of the Bunker Convention (replaces the 1958 Act equivalent)', which reads as India being a Party. IMO Status of Treaties (26 Aug 2026) does not list India under BUNKERS 2001. The reg-desc now states the Act as India's domestic regime (ss.198, 204, 205, 206-207, read in the Gazette text) and that India is not a Party; the unverified 1958-equivalent limb is removed. Convention-level teaching elsewhere on the card is jurisdiction-neutral and unchanged. Stamped v1.2.
changed_propositions: Reg-box MS Act 2025 Part IX Ch IV: 'domestic implementation of the Bunker Convention (replaces the 1958 Act equivalent)' -> India's domestic bunker-oil liability regime modelled on the Convention; India not a Party.
q-version v1.1 -> v1.2 (prior 15 Jul 2026 note retained in the stamp).

The FAL / PANS card taught a '96-hour advance arrival notification (SOLAS XI-2 / ISPS Code)', PANS sent to a 'DGS port office', a reg-box '96-hour submission to DGS', and an unconditional 96 hours in the CE tip, numbers box and memory map. MS Notice 13 of 2024 (still listed by DGMA): to the port / PFSO and the regional Navy JOC or Coast Guard MRCC at least 96 hours before arrival, or within 2 hours of departure on a shorter voyage; 96 hours set by the 2024 national Rules. Every PANS site now carries the rule and its condition; the SOLAS limb states only the power to require information before entry. The SQ copy is a locked teaser and is unchanged. Stamped v1.1.
changed_propositions: Body: SOLAS/ISPS 96-hour notification -> SOLAS XI-2/9.2 power to require information before entry; India's period set by national rules.
Body: 'ships notify DGS port office 96 hours before arrival' -> PANS under MS Notice 13 of 2024, recipients, at least 96 h / within 2 h of departure, ship types, form contents (FAL Forms 5 and 7).
Reg-box: SOLAS item without a 96-hour figure; 'DGS MS Notice - 96-hour submission to DGS' -> MS Notice 13 of 2024 with recipients, the conditional rule and the Rules as source of the 96 hours.
CE tip, numbers box, memory map: conditional rule stated.
